summary: Round 6 plan check, 05:45-05:55Z on 26 Sep. Nothing here needs a build, push or submit. State is sound. CLARIFICATION v3 (fc51b75, 04:04:45Z) and the K2'' builder change (801de5a/2f6ec9d, 04:12Z) were committed and pushed before any score (HEAD == origin/main). The poller (PID 20052) is alive; its last poll was 05:43:54Z, and its next polls around the mark are ~07:54:2x and ~08:04:2x. The clean-proof job _dl/clean_proof_polls.py (PID 13436) has run since 04:04:37Z, stamps after each call and caps stamps at 08:02:10Z. The laptop is on AC. #37/#38 are still PENDING (L > 5.69 h), and no user answer to the 04:04Z OK request is recorded. Memory files are current. Six gaps remain; the first must be written before the twin can score (~06:15Z onward). (1) CONTEXT has no rule on when an [OK] counts. The 0.952 twin floor becomes a post-hoc choice if the OK arrives after the twin's 0.952 is visible. (2) The V4 bound B, which drives the K2'' recommendation, is anti-conservative by ~0.7 h. Across 10 x138-family dummies the GPU prediction phase varies by up to 15.4% (9.18-10.59 min) and setup by 0.13 h, but 6.56 h only adds 0.1 h. The 72.5 s/clip insertion cost is a 4-clip mean, not a max. (3) The READ TABLE's blanket 'R5(b) admits K2 and the twin unless they ERROR' rests on F = 7.87 h, which has no run-to-run variance. Corrected: F' = min(L35_hi, L36_hi) + 0.14 + 0.71 = 8.27 h. The 1 h margin still holds, but only through L36 (with L35 alone the margin would be 0.92 h). No clause covers an observed L(K2) that contradicts the forecast. (4) The K2'' dummy gate (CSV sha == K2 dummy) cannot catch a mis-build, because a K2 rebuilt by mistake gives the same CSV. (5) _dl/oneshot_poll.py stamps BEFORE its call. Used by hand in 07:45-08:05Z, it can fake a 'clean' K2. (6) ledger.md says 'keep the poller alive until 08:32:12Z', which contradicts V7, and V7 does not cover submissions made later today (K1/K2''/resubmit). K3/K3b/forkblob/K4 stay closed; nothing is proposed for them.

findings.what: No rule in CONTEXT says when an [OK] item counts. The 'OK given after a visible score is post-hoc' principle appears only in round-4/5 reports and WATCHLIST W45; there is no CONTEXT line. The OK request was posted at 04:04Z, the user's reply is not recorded, and the twin can score any time from ~06:15Z (user local time UTC+3). Some [OK] items read a score: the 0.952 twin floor (row 3), row-2 'F2 = K2 if d1 >= -0.001', and K1 in rows 4/C4. If the reply arrives after poll.log shows the scores those items depend on, accepting the OK is selection by result. The clearest case is 'twin = 0.952' followed by 'yes to the floor'. Other items respond to events, not scores, and are legitimately OK'd afterwards: the C2(a) Kaggle Error resubmit, K1 after a K2 exception (row 1/C2(c)), and K2'' after the runtime trigger.

findings.what: The V4 runtime bound B = min(L(K2)_hi, L(K2)_hi - L(twin)_lo + 6.56 h, L(twin)_hi + 1.95 h) decides the K2'' band (<= 8.0 ~0 value; 8.0-9.0 optional; > 9.0 recommend). It is anti-conservative by ~0.7 h. (a) '6.56 = L34_hi 6.46 + 0.1 h jitter' covers only the setup spread. The GPU prediction phase itself varies up to 15.4% between identical x138-family runs (dummy logs 'Prediction completed in': exp57b 9.18, K1 9.22, FD 9.28, K2 9.30, twin 9.40, exp51 9.68, exp48 9.70, FF 10.07, exp56 10.59 min). At ~140 s/clip GPU on the hidden run: 0.154*140*97/3600 = 0.58 h. Setup ('Launching 2 independent video shards' at 258-704 s) adds 0.13 h. (b) The third term assumes K2's and the twin's GPU phases are equally fast, which needs the same +0.71 h. (c) '97 x 72.5 s' is the MEAN insertion cost over the 4 dummy clips (per clip K2-twin repair = 36.2/62.7/9.6/181.9 s), not a maximum; it agrees with the step-0 estimate of ~66 s/clip, so keep it but call it an estimate. (d) F (7.87 h) adds 4.45 s/clip for lowrefine while B assumes ~0. The dummies show lowrefine's repair cost is noise (twin 218.8 s vs exp56 226.5 s; K2 509.2 vs K1 499.8 vs exp57b 491.4). This inconsistency is harmless but should be resolved conservatively (+0.14 h). Consequence: B as written can say 'the insertion gate very likely never fired, K2'' ~0 value' when K2's own runtime could be ~0.7 h longer.

If the user's OK item 5 (K2'' when B > 9.0 h) is given, it acts on B as approved. If B <= 9.0 h < B', do not act; ask the user and show both numbers.' Worked example: L(K2) in (8.1, 8.3], L(twin) in (7.4, 7.6] gives B = 7.46 but B' = 8.21 h (band 'optional', not '~0 value').

findings.what: The READ TABLE line 'R5: F(K2) = 7.87 h leaves 1.63 h to the 9.5 h repair deadline, so R5(b) admits K2 and the twin unless they ERROR' is a blanket judgment. It is not conditioned on what the LB later shows. R5(b) needs a step-0 forecast with >= 1 h margin. With run-to-run variance (PC6-02), F from L35_hi is 7.73 + 0.14 + 0.71 = 8.58 h, a 0.92 h margin, which FAILS the 1 h clause. Only the P36 anchor (L36_hi 7.42 h; P36 = #35 stack + leaf prune, same runtime class) gives F' = 7.42 + 0.14 + 0.71 = 8.27 h, a 1.23 h margin, which passes. Also, if K2 is still PENDING past 09:32:12Z (L(K2)_lo > 9.5 h), the ledger will print 'R5(a) FAILS' plus the stale A6/K1 text. The blanket would still admit K2 even when the paired observation (B') says K2's own runtime may have exceeded 9.5 h, which is exactly when the degrade fired on the last-sorted (private) clips. Probability is low (it needs queue > ~2 h or a slow K2 run), but the rule should be written before K2 scores.

findings.what: The V3 gate for K2'' ('a K2'' dummy whose CSV sha256 equals the K2 dummy CSV') cannot detect a mis-build. On the 4 dummy clips no deadline fires (K2 kernel end 1,512 s), so a K2 rebuilt by mistake, or an exp58d with deadlines that did not take, produces the same CSV and passes. tools/dummy_gates.py has no K2'' mode. The K2 log already prints the knob line ('SAFETAIL: repair deadline 34200s, divins deadline 28800s, keep_div_after_deadline=1, divins_force_fail=0'), so a direct check is cheap. There is a second trap. C2(a) says 'resubmit K2 v1 unchanged'. Pushing K2'' as a new VERSION of the K2 slug (biohub-exp58-x138-safe-lowref) would make that resubmit, or any later look at 'K2', ambiguous.

findings.what: _dl/oneshot_poll.py, an older ad-hoc poll helper, stamps its header BEFORE the CLI call (ts taken first, then subprocess.run with timeout=180). The ledger treats a COMPLETE row as first seen at the header time. If the main session runs this helper by hand at, say, 08:01:5x and the call returns after 08:02:12Z with K2 COMPLETE, K2 would be graded 'clean' (L_hi <= 8.0 h) when that is not proven. The same stamp-before-call applies to lb_poll.py. That is harmless there only because its polls land at ~07:54 and ~08:04, far from the mark.

findings.what: C2(d) sends 'Notebook Timeout / Exceeded Allowed Compute on K2 only' to 'ask the user; default row 1 [OK]' (= K1). K1 is not an independent retry for a runtime failure. It carries the same insertion, the same 8.0 h insertion gate and the same 9.5 h repair deadline, and differs from K2 only by lowrefine, which has no measurable runtime cost. K2'' would make a timeout more likely, not less. A K2-only timeout despite the 9.5 h degrade points to a hang in a stage that K1 shares, unless lowrefine's coordinate changes altered the ILP/relink. Probability is very low (~<1%).
